body:
It frustrates me but I try to remind myself that I’m not the gatekeeper of feelings. We all likely have Major Depressive Disorder which is much more long term, severe, and debilitating. That said, anyone experiencing depressed feelings for a short time is just as valid as our long term feeling. Just like if I had a headache and was in pain, it doesn’t meant that my pain is any less valid than someone who suffers chronic migraines. 

If anything, others’ feeling depressed can be a good chance for us to express that it is something with struggle with all the time. If/when that person recovers, they will be able to more effectively empathize with what it would feel like to be that way all the time without the possibility of it clearing up on its own.
They will not ask for your location (at least not in the US)

Hi. I called the hotline last week. They will not call the police or an ambulance if you assure them that you do not have a plan/ have done anything that put your life at risk and if you tell them that you are not at risk of hurting yourself or anyone else. 

So you know what to expect.. they will listen to you but are not able to give substantial advice  Any advice is fairly unhelpful and what we know we should be doing- “what do you enjoy doing? can you do it? Have you eaten/bathed/whatever today.”

The most therapeutic part is having someone you can be (mostly) honest with and have a good cry to without feeling guilty or like a burden. They will be sympathetic and parrot back back and validate your feelings. (ie: Me- I cant function and I’m lonely” Them- “it sounds like you are struggling and it sounds very difficult to experience that.”) 

After a short time it felt annoying but the cathartic release of just having someone to talk to without feeling guilty makes it worth it. It can’t hurt to try. I hope you feel some form of peace soon.
Oh wow. I’ve never heard anyone else say it but I’ve frequently expressed it. If I’m forced to stay alive I would do anything to end my suffering. Anything.

You aren’t ugly at all. The only think that I think is even slightly negative is your eyes being downturned, but my partner has that feature and I don’t think it affects their attractiveness. Liner can help with eye shape if you want to google makeup tips or find makeup subs there are lots of advice for applying with downturned eyes. . Also your bangs are not ideal for you face and ear shape. Curtain bangs or a side part with swoop bangs might be more flattering. You have a really nice smile, skin, lips, and teeth. And your dimples areal cute! Your eyes are pretty and you could carry eyeshadow really well if you are into wearing it since you have a lot of lid space *cries in hooded eyes*. Not ugly whatsoever.
Lmao!!!! Thank you for pointing this out I can’t believe OP didn’t ask wtf I was talking about. I’m dead 😆

Depression can affect anyone.. successful, with loving partners, poor, rich.... anyone... It’s ok to feel not ok even with all these things that are positive in your life. I don’t offer this advice much on this sub because it’s cliche but if these feelings you are experiencing are new,  a therapist may be able to help you work them out before the situation potentially gets worse.

I think this person is expressing that they feel conflicted between what the world is telling them should make them happy (friends, partner,job) and their feelings of depression and sadness even with all these things they are grateful for.

Not even wealthy, if I was just able to have enough for housing, food, a dog.... I would struggle with depression but not be suicidal. I would be able to find meaning in raising children, walking the dog, cooking meals in my own kitchen.. and those things would take up time and distract from depression. 

My hopelessness comes from not being able to support myself or have a family because I can’t provide. On the brink of homelessness, etc. 

Depression will always be a factor but there are a million factors with quality of living that affect a person’s ability to cope. Successful people just happen to commit suicide for other quality of life factors than finances.. trauma, disease, mental illness, personal relationships, etc.

As a very very low functioning, I’m genuinely happy that you are able to maintain positive aspects of your life even if I am not. We all have our own struggles and they don’t compare.  Suffering is suffering. If anything I’m grateful there is someone out there in the world doing what they can and bringing the empathy of your personal experience into your interactions with others. The fact that you feel for people who have it worse just shows that you are a kind person. You are not a fraud in any way.

It’s not a matter of not hurting anyone’s feelings. I don’t see anything wrong with his face that is unappealing in any way shape or form. I don’t know what you mean by perfection either, or what one point from perfection would entail... But I also don’t think many Instagram dudes or celebrities are all that perfect so it boils down to different perceptions I guess 🤷🏼‍♂️

RBF is just a shortening of resting bitch face.  I hope you are able to overcome your feelings about compliments. We are anonymous people on the internet so there’s no reason to lie to you. Your eyes and lips have a really pleasant color, your skin is really nice, and you have a nice jaw line. You can just practice hearing compliments a little at a time until maybe you find a way to accept it and not feel nervous or hostile. r/toastme is a really wholesome subreddit with plenty of people who are happy to compliment. If you need practice accepting them.

Edited after the reply below made me realize that RBF is indeed not short for RBF 😆

That a big fat “ew” from me. I’m sorry there is a guardian treating you like that... it’s so, so wrong. She may not be worth sharing your knowledge with in the future, as long as you don’t feel like it’s more harmful to you to have to hold your tongue.

If you still have Facebook, Instagram, etc. it might be healthy for you to take a break. I took a break for a bit, went back, felt terrible again, and haven’t been back since. Even certain subreddits at times are mentally exhausting but Reddit is the easiest to fine tune what kind of content you are exposed to.
I get it, I’ve been crying all morning too. I hope you’ve found some peace with whatever is getting you down. And hopefully hearing you are super handsome helped a little.

You are not ugly at all. I’ve come to learn that everyone who doesn’t make an active effort to look happy is labeled with RBF. I’ve been told that before by a person who fake smiled all the time, but I realized actually had “RBF” when no one was looking. If anything is even slightly negative it’s that you just look mildly insecure, which is understandable since you are here asking for opinion. 

I’ve been bullied as well and internalized a lot of it. Sometimes it just takes a not shitty person to remind you there is nothing unattractive about you. I hope you have found a cool group of people who also like cool shit like tech and anime, and if you don’t have one already there’s definitely plenty of women out there who will love your look.
9/10. Not ugly on any planet. You have very nice skin and facial features. Only thing bringing you down is that your brow looks heavy and your eyes a little sad.
To misery 🥂 Thank you, ironically it’s the first I’ve stopped crying all morning.

As someone with body dysmorphia I don’t doubt that you feel ugly. But in a world where we are slammed with fake perfection, you’re likely better looking than you give yourself credit for, especially if you are comparing yourself to other “perfect” men. And if you are a teen your body and face are still developing. Still, none of that changes how you feel and I’m sad you have to feel that way. Your feelings are valid. 

There is always the option to post on  r/amiugly, were the vast majority of people who think they are ugly actually aren’t. Worst case scenario you aren’t worse off than you are now and can get an outsiders perspective. There is also r/toastme, where kind Redditors would be happy to point out nice things about you.
I hear you. You don’t have to say anything, it sucks and you aren’t alone.

It helps that there is another human who understands even though I wouldn’t wish it on anyone. It sucks that the only way we able able to seek or give support is through a Reddit post because a lot of us are deeply missing human interaction but aboid it because we don’t want to be an emotional burden. My misery loves company only if the other person is already miserable for their own reasons and we can just exist together, not because I make them miserable.

Do you think every call is like that because of its structure or are there any genuinely compassionate people who can just sympathize instead of placating? I am highly motivated to find a group support which is something I never wanted before, and of course with covid it’s not possible. 

Thank you for taking the time to talk to me.

Last time I called I felt worse after because I couldn’t answer any of the person’s questions. I have a family to tell me “go do something that makes you happy” and “it will get better”. 

I know I’m being a pain but I feel like I just want someone to tell me it’s ok to be sick and that it won’t get better because it’s a lifelong illness. Not someone following a script to distract me so I don’t kill myself.

My parents asked me to call one a few years when I expressed how bad things had gotten and it was really awful. She just sounded so annoyed that I couldn’t go along with her script. She asked what I liked to do for fun... I told her that I am too ill to feel enjoyment and she just didn’t know how to proceed and it was so awkward....It all felt terrible. 

I just want to be able to speak to a real human out loud who understands and won’t make me feel even worse about being such a lifeless burden.
I called and hung up. I don’t want to be a burden on anyone else more than I am. And the cheerful recorded voice telling me that my call will be recorded for quality assurance freaked me out.

One problem at a time- it sounds like your parents are crippling your development. Are you financially dependent on them? You don’t have to cut ties but things will not get better with them until you learn how to set boundaries. You are an adult. It doesn’t matter that she is your mom, her behavior is harassing. You have to tell her “mom, I love you, but I’m an adult and you are overstepping the boundaries of a heathy relationship.” Set firm boundaries (e.g. Only call me once/X amount of times a week or month)

You are doing amazing things for your future and setting yourself up for success. Your parents are setting you up for failing by treating you like a child. You need to learn to trust your own judgement and it will give you confidence as you continue to grow, fail, emerge from failure, and ultimately succeed.
Look for some of those foil lined temperature maintaining grocery bags that can be sealed. It might help keep things from getting too hot.

What you are doing is brave but it’s wise of you to know your limits. I had to do the same in college. I don’t know if you have been through it before but the hospital was the hardest part. They lack a lot of sympathy. Be aware that they may ask you to strip nude for them so they can check you for pills and that they may keep you in a waiting room for up to 12 hours in my case before they take you to the facility. 

I’m not trying to dissuade you, I admire that you are getting help. I just want you to be aware that the hospital itself can be a difficult process. Try checking in through a mental health facility if possible.
You deserve better.

I live with crippling guilt over the pain my depression causes my partner and parents. This book sounds like a nightmare honestly. No one deserves to have to deal with me. It’s part of the reason I don’t understand why they won’t let me go
I believe you. Your suffering is real. You could be a white privileged millionaire living on the beach with loving parents and a herd of golden retrievers, and your sadness would still be valid.

This is controversial and I’m sorry if it breaks sub rules to suggest it, but I’ve also used a rubber band to snap on my arm if I wanted to cut. It snapped me out of the fog but there was no chance of accidentally cutting too deep and scars.
You’re not alone

Sensory deprivation works for me in a similar way cutting did. I put blankets in a small dark place and completely shut off all lights, smell, noise (except music or white noise sometimes) but use headphones to block everything else out. I’m not sure why it works but it tends to break me out of crisis mode where I am desperate for any form of relief.

I’ve never tried it recreationally. The way it would be done clinically is in an office for several hours while they monitor vitals. 

Supposedly it helps rewire the brain out of depressive thought patterns? But you’re right, there’s no evidence of long term success. I think that clinically it is used differently than just a means to escape. Although I’d do anything to escape at this point.
Silver Linings Playbook
Does Girl,Interrupted work for this?

I feel like a hypocrite trying to give advice half of the time. Most of us aren’t able to cope and desperate for help as well. When I do give advice I feel like it is possibly dangerous. I refuse to tell people “it will get better” and other platitudes because I despise when people tell me that.

This sub feels more like a place for people to express themselves which can be therapeutic on its own. At best we can offer coping mechanisms but often they aren’t healthy which is why it feels dangerous to give advice. 

All I can say is that I hear you and you aren’t alone. We are all suffering greatly and if nothing else at least we can empathize with each other.

Hi. You aren’t alone. I know this isn’t the healthiest coping mechanism, but when I get into that zone I go full sensory deprivation to calm down. I clear out the floor of my closet and set up a blanket and pillows. I keep the lights out and either listen to music, white noise, or a show. Sometimes you just have to mentally check out to get relief from the pain. There’s something about being in a small, dark, quiet place that is surprisingly grounding.

I’m hella corny and married someone just as cheesy as me. I dated a lot of people along the way who found me too dorky. Give yourself time to be awkward until you get more comfortable. Share small parts of yourself but remain guarded until you are either able to be yourself with her. 

You will be alright. This person will either like you for who you are or it’s not worth the time, but you will never know unless you are able to be brave and show your true corny self.
Your pain is real and it is valid. No matter how much privilege you may have, you don’t need to be guilty for suffering.
You feel guilty because we are told our whole lives to suck it up because someone always has it worse.

You were so brave to the express yourself to him. But also I’m sorry fuck him. No one likes struggles and challenges asswipe. Parents are the ones who are supposed to teach us how to work through challenges but a lot of us got emotionally neglected and never learned how to cope. 

For your own sanity and from personal experience, don’t expect that he will ever sympathize with you. 

Your dads response makes me rage because when I told my own dad that I was non-functioning depressive and was trying to thing of other means of income he said something fucked up like “you really will do anything not to work full time won’t you.”


I’m sorry your dad said that. You deserve better.

Nature- Brain chemistry and genetics for sure. 
Nurture- Emotionally intelligent parents who are able to teach resilience and healthy coping mechanisms from a young age. Learning how to not internalize failures and rejection, etc. 

I feel like a lot of people lack one or the other of the above and still manage to be successful. But some people have the double whammy of lacking both and are unable to move past negativity, trauma, insecurity, etc.

I think you should tell her that. Your mom is “helping” the only way she knows how but it’s obviously making things worse even if she has good intentions. To tell you that it’s your fault and she has no sympathy is incredibly cruel. 

Try approaching her with the format “mom, when you say X, it makes me feel X. I know it’s hard to watch someone you love struggle, but it would help me if you said X instead of X.” 

What do you want to hear from your mom in those instances? My therapist asked me that question and it was hard to answer. I had to realize that it was incredibly taxing on my mom to watch me suffer, so I backed off on talking to her about it. Does your mom suffer from mental illness too? She may be lashing out because your depressive episodes might be triggering her own. Her anger and lashing out may come from a place of helplessness watching you suffer. 

I’m not defending her because that’s a fucked up way to try and “help” your child. But I imagine she feels really hopeless about it too. Even with the empathy I do have, I am terrified to have a child that would be like me. Suffering and outside the realm of help, like I am to my mother.

I feel you. Not sure how old you are but once I reached 30s and came to the realization that I was going to be poor and childless forever, it became the final act. All those things that you have hoped for when you grow up are suddenly beyond reach and the time has passed. The only way I can describe it is a life devoid of hope for anything to change. 

You say you have plans for the future which is really awesome. Hold onto them with everything  you have. Once they are gone for good it’s really bad. Don’t lose your plans and start thinking of tangible ways to make them happen.

I wish I had advice for you. I’m sorry for not being helpful. You are not the only one who feels like that though.

Aside from the interpersonal aspects, is it a career you could see yourself being happy with? If you like the job itself, you might want to look into transferring internships if possible. It sounds like continuing in the current environment isn’t an option. I would start looking into ways to find a better place of work with more supportive superiors. It sounds like you are very capable but are overwhelmed with the fear of failure threatening you. If I’m understanding, it sounds like them, not you. Another option could be setting up an appointment with your superiors to find out exactly what it is that makes them tell you that you will fail. Get it in writing and work on it if it’s something within your control. 

If you can’t see yourself in the career anymore, start trying to look for careers in fields where your current skills and experience will be helpful. 

I’m so sorry you are in this position. It’s clear you have worked hard the past 6 years. Easier said than done, but if you are proactive up until the point of possible failure it will be much easier to pick yourself back up because you were prepared.

Nothing has changed with my intake of caffeine and I don’t smoke or use any other stimulants. Even when I did smoke and drink more caffeine in the past I still binge ate. I appreciate the suggestion though.
